abstract.p: The ability of generative large language models (LLMs) to perform in-context learning has given rise to a large body of research into how best to prompt models for various natural language processing tasks. In this paper, we focus on machine translation (MT), a task that has been shown to benefit from in-context translation examples. However no systematic studies have been published on how best to select examples, and mixed results have been reported on the usefulness of similarity-based selection over random selection, although these results have mainly been shown for high-resource languages only. We provide a study covering multiple LLMs and in-context example retrieval strategies. Contrarily to previously published results, we find that retrieval based on sentence embedding similarity can improve MT, especially for low-resource language directions, and we also discuss the balance between selection pool diversity and quality. 1
